newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia cuts official interest rates.
newsitem.headline: Australia cuts official interest rates.

text.p: The Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) said on Wednesday it was cutting official interest rates by half a percentage point to 6.5 percent.
Rates were last cut on July 31, when the official cash rate was brought down to 7.0 percent from 7.5 percent.
Australian markets were expecting a rate cut after recent data showing a sluggish economy and weak employment market combined with low inflation and moderate wages growth.
Announcing its second rate cut this year, the RBA said the outlook for inflation had improved and this had increased scope for a faster rate of economic growth.
The RBA pointed to exchange rate stability as another factor in its decision, but added that it was still concerned by the level of some wage claims.

"I guess we were looking for a cut this morning, given the weakness in the retail trade figures...and the continued weak outlook for employment and the fact that the inflation and wages numbers were pretty good," said ANZ Banking Group economist Karen Pringle.
